title: SASHA Privacy Policy
intro: This Privacy Policy explains how SASHA processes account, business, integration, and limited customer information. It is a working draft and must be reviewed by qualified legal counsel before broad commercial release.

sections.title: 1. Information we collect
paragraphs: We collect user account information such as name, email address, organization, role, authentication events, and policy acceptances. We process business data from systems an authorized user connects, including operational, reservation, sales, marketing, advertising, analytics, and integration metadata.

sections.title: 2. Credentials and connected accounts
paragraphs: Connection credentials and revocable authorization tokens are encrypted in a secrets vault and are not displayed after storage. We record non-secret connection status, mappings, validation times, and import results to operate and troubleshoot integrations.

sections.title: 3. Reservation contact information
paragraphs: Some approved automations may retrieve customer contact information from a connected reservation system for immediate use, such as sending a class-status notice. Phone numbers used by the low-reservation alert automation are processed transiently and are not stored in SASHA delivery logs. Logs retain non-contact delivery evidence such as class, studio, status, and timestamps.

sections.title: 4. How we use information
paragraphs: We use information to authenticate users, provide dashboards and reporting, run configured integrations and automations, secure the platform, diagnose errors, preserve audit history, support users, and improve service reliability. We do not use connected business data for unrelated consumer advertising.

sections.title: 5. Service providers and disclosures
paragraphs: We may use infrastructure, database, authentication, orchestration, messaging, analytics, and support providers to operate SASHA. Information may also be disclosed when required by law, to protect rights and security, in a business transaction subject to appropriate safeguards, or at the direction of the organization controlling the workspace.

sections.title: 6. Benchmarking
paragraphs: Privacy-protected reciprocal benchmarking is optional and defaults off. When enabled by an authorized organization administrator, only aggregated results meeting configured cohort thresholds are returned. Participation can be withdrawn without affecting prior lawful processing or preserved consent history.

sections.title: 7. Retention
paragraphs: Business records and historical reporting data are retained according to the organization agreement and documented retention practices. Security, import, and consent records may be retained longer when needed for legal compliance, dispute resolution, fraud prevention, or platform integrity. Secrets are removed or revoked when a connection is deleted or access is terminated, subject to operational backup periods.

sections.title: 8. Security
paragraphs: We use access controls, tenant scoping, encrypted transport, encrypted secret storage, session limits, audit records, and service-role boundaries designed to protect information. No system can guarantee absolute security, and users must protect their accounts and promptly report suspected compromise.

sections.title: 9. Choices and requests
paragraphs: Authorized users may update profile information and disconnect integrations. Individuals and organizations may request access, correction, export, or deletion as applicable by contacting the service operator. Certain records may be retained when required for security, contractual, or legal purposes.

sections.title: 10. Changes and contact
paragraphs: Material policy changes will receive a new version and require renewed acceptance before continued dashboard access. Privacy questions and requests should be directed to the privacy contact published by the service operator.
